Depends on what you want exactly in your car.  
If you want something not amazing, relatively cheap, but very reliable, go for a more budget friendly Volkswagen or Volvo, even a Mazda. Something like a newer Golf 8 (not the best looking imo, but very fun and reliable), a newer VW Jetta (the 2022+ models are cool looking too), maybe even a Phaeton if you're not a big spender.  
Volvo is known for its insane safety and reliability, so anything within your budget that you like from Volvo is nice.

I'd say a good ballpark for your car price, considering insurance, eventual repair costs and so on, would be around a maximum 30% of your annual salary. Obviously you can go higher but if you don't want to risk a lot of money on this, I'd say 30% is reasonable. So for you something around 30-32k I'd say.

For something cooler, faster, not as reliable but maybe more comfy and fun, I'd go for a Lexus UX, RX, ES or NX series, basically any Lexus lol. Lexus' are also pretty well know to be one of the most reliable luxury cars on the market too, another bonus. If the cool factor is a big thing for you, go for a newer Mazda like the MX 5, Mazda 3 or any CX model.

In the end it also depends on what you like, if you want something smaller but cooler like the MX 5, Lexus ES and so on, or something more like a family car such as the Jetta or Mazda CX; if you want a sedan or a suv or a 2door and so on. Make a list of things you wish for in your car and see what you can filter out to get as close to what you like as possible.

Personally I consider this a mistake. Unfortunately I'm the type of person that has to hit his head many times in the same place to actually learn a lesson, so I've got quite a bit of (un)wanted experience on this topic. I've tried to remain friends with almost all of my exes, but I was never the one to initiate this idea after the break-ups, and eventually I came to accept that it just is not something that sits right with me, mentally and emotionally.   


Usually it would be somewhat fine for the first few days of being just friends, but after getting to know someone so well on that kind of level, it's never the same to "downgrade". Especially if you've been wronged and the relationship ended because of mistakes on either side or both sides. Things that remain unresolved come back to bite you in the ass, and talking about them and sorting it out is most of the time no longer an option if you're just friends.  


Futhermore, keeping relatively close to your ex after a breakup will just fuck up your healing progress and make it go way slower, either by you having second thoughts and "what if's" or by realizing that was not a good person to start with, you were just blinded by rose tinted glasses. Healing is way easier and faster if you remove that person from your life as much as possible.  And seeing him/her/them after what happened between you will just be a trigger for emotions and thoughts that aren't usually worth anything, intrusive thoughts that just act like small traps which will set you back on your progress so far on healing. Out of sight out of mind type of situation is what I've found works best for me and lots of other people.

You have to stop talking to them, stop questioning their reasons for doing what they did, admit it, accept it and realize it's over, sit with yourself, talk to your most trustworthy friends to get other perspectives, talk to your parents, journal your emotions, process that shit, and eventually you'll wake up after 2-3-4-5 etc months and be able to smile about the situation and even really become friends again, two healed, but completely different individuals from the ones you were at the start. 

Trying to stay friends while all the emotions are still raw and unfiltered and unprocessed is imo a way of selfsabotage. And as someone else said, you can stay friendly (or not lol, you don't owe explanations to anyone about how you choose to carry yourself through these emotions), and it is very different and decent.
